scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a config-cleanup window, a user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports they
lost all reach across the fabric -- pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is unreachable,
though pc_0_1 can still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1. Both spine
routers report their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_1 down at the
same time, yet leaf_router_0_1's uplink interfaces show UP and its FRR
daemons are all running. Investigate.

injection.action: delete both spine neighbor statements from the running BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 BGP neighbor configuration
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1 (AS 65201) normally peers with
  spine_router_0_0 (neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100) and
  spine_router_0_1 (neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101). Both
  neighbor statements were deleted from the running config, so bgpd
  sends a Cease notification and drops both sessions. With zero peers
  the leaf stops advertising 10.0.1.0/24 (the spines withdraw it
  immediately) and stops learning 10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_1 is isolated
  even though bgpd is running and every link is UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both BGP neighbor statements removed under
  `router bgp 65201` on leaf_router_0_1
Fix: re-add the two neighbor statements on leaf_router_0_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the spine neighbors on leaf_router_0_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65201"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on leaf_router_0_1 is an equally correct fix (it reloads the file and
re-creates both neighbors).
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BGP neighbor configuration removed / no configured peers
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: uplink interfaces UP and bgpd running while both spine sessions are down -- a config fault, not a link or daemon fault
bonus-cites-missing-neighbors: names the missing neighbor statements (172.16.0.6 / spine_router_0_0 and 172.16.0.10 / spine_router_0_1) or shows `show bgp summary` with zero peers

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the BGP control-plane on leaf_router_0_1 (FRR bgpd configuration). Both spines show their sessions to leaf_router_0_1 stuck in Active, indicating they are attempting but failing to establish TCP/BGP. On spine_router_0_0 and spine_router_0_1, “show ip bgp summary” lists neighbors 172.16.0.7 and 172.16.0.11 (leaf uplinks) in Active. Meanwhile, leaf_router_0_1 itself reports “% No BGP neighbors found in VRF default,” and its running-config under “router bgp 65201” has no neighbor statements at all. Its interfaces eth0 (172.16.0.7/31) and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31) are UP, confirming the issue is not at Layer 1/2.

Mechanism: Without BGP neighbors configured on the leaf, no eBGP sessions come up, so 10.0.1.0/24 is not advertised to the spines and the leaf learns no path to 10.0.0.0/24. This isolates pc_0_1 behind leaf_router_0_1: it can ping its gateway (10.0.1.1 on eth2) but cannot reach pc_0_0 across the fabric.

Localization: leaf_router_0_1, FRR bgpd process/config; uplinks eth0/eth1 toward the spines.

Root cause: BGP neighbor configuration lines on leaf_router_0_1 were removed during the “config-cleanup” window.

Corrective fix: Re-add BGP neighbors on leaf_router_0_1:
- neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100 (to spine_router_0_0)
- neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101 (to spine_router_0_1)
Ensure address-family ipv4 unicast is active with network 10.0.1.0/24 and “no bgp ebgp-requires-policy” present. Commit/save the config. This will restore sessions and end-to-end reachability.

Proposes re-adding the two missing BGP neighbors on leaf_router_0_1 (with saving and IPv4 address-family/network considerations), which matches the expected fix.
